caveats: With 6 vs 6, a rank-sum test has a floor on its p-value; a set can be robust and still not reach a small p
Leave-one-out is a fragility diagnostic, not a validation — a set surviving it is still a single-cohort finding
ssGSEA-type scores are relative within the sample set and are not comparable to scores computed on another cohort
steps.context: T1S2 gives one enrichment statistic per hallmark from a single group-level contrast and cannot say whether the signal is uniform across the 6 lesional samples. Because the raw counts are supplied, per-sample scoring is available and is the cheapest meaningful robustness check for an n=6 vs n=6 design with one flagged low-depth library (sample_01). This step does not replace T1S2 — it qualifies which of its calls survive sample-level scrutiny.
steps.question: Are the significant hallmark enrichments consistent across all 6 lesional samples, or are they driven by a minority of samples (including the low-depth sample_01)?
constraints: Normalize for library size before scoring so sample_01's low depth is not read as low pathway activity — state the normalization used
Use the same human hallmark collection resolved in T1S2, so scores and enrichment refer to identical gene sets
Report Wilcoxon results with n=6 per group as what they are: the minimum attainable p-value is bounded, so present effect sizes alongside p-values rather than p-values alone
Do not use the per-sample scores to define new significant hallmarks not tested in T1S2 without labelling that as exploratory
steps.description: Per-sample hallmark activity scoring to test the robustness of the T1S2 result. From counts.csv, build a normalized expression matrix (VST or log-CPM with library-size normalization, so that sample_01's ~4x-lower depth does not dominate) and compute single-sample scores for the hallmark sets that reached padj<0.05 in T1S2 — using an installed single-sample method (decoupler's ssGSEA/AUCell/mean-z, GSVA, or singscore). Sets that fail leave-one-out must be labelled fragile in the summary.
acceptance_criteria: Sample x hallmark score matrix computed for every hallmark set significant in T1S2 (and, if fewer than 5 were significant, for all 50), with the scoring method named
Heatmap saved with samples annotated by condition and library size, sample_01 identifiable
Per-hallmark lesional-vs-control Wilcoxon p-values with BH adjustment and an effect size reported in a table
Leave-one-out results reported for every T1S2-significant set, naming each set whose group difference loses significance when a single sample is dropped and identifying which sample
A written summary classifying each significant hallmark as robust or fragile with respect to single-sample removal

plan.title: Hallmark GSEA of psoriasis lesional vs control
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question is narrow: which MSigDB hallmark pathways change between the treated (psoriasis lesional) and control skin samples. Differential expression is already done and supplied as /data/inputs/results/de_results.csv (12,000 genes x 8 columns, DESeq2 treated vs control), so no re-running of DESeq2 is planned. The primary work is therefore a rank-based hallmark GSEA (T1S2) on the full 12,000-gene ranking, using the staged human hallmark collection (MSigDB 2026.1, 50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols) — the correct organism file, since the data are Homo sapiens skin.

Two things justify the small amount of work that precedes it. First, the DE table must be sanity-checked before it is trusted as a ranking: the profile flags that sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, which in a 6 vs 6 unpaired design is enough to distort dispersion estimates and shrunken fold changes if that sample is a control-side outlier. T1S1 therefore does a compact QC/consistency check — VST/CPM PCA and library-size summary from counts.csv against metadata.csv, plus verification that the supplied de_results.csv is internally coherent (p-value distribution, padj vs pvalue monotonicity, log2FC vs baseMean shape) and that its gene identifier space matches the counts. This is diagnostic, not a re-analysis, and its output is an explicit statement of whether the ranking is fit for GSEA and whether sample_01 drives it.

Second, GSEA on a single pre-computed contrast gives one number per hallmark set with no sample-level resolution. T1S3 complements it with per-sample single-sample scoring (ssGSEA/AUCell-style, from the same counts matrix) for the hallmark sets that came out significant, which shows whether a set's enrichment is consistent across all 6 lesional samples or driven by one or two — the single most common way a hallmark result from n=6 per group turns out to be fragile, and directly checkable here because the counts are supplied.

The ranking metric for T1S2 is the signed test statistic (or, failing that, sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue)), not log2FC alone, because with 12,000 genes and shrunken fold changes an unweighted log2FC ranking loses the precision information. Multiple testing is over 50 sets only, so BH-adjusted p-values will be reported for all 50 rather than a filtered subset — with 50 hallmarks the full table is the honest output. Directionality (NES sign) is reported explicitly with respect to the stated treated-vs-control contrast direction, since a sign error here silently inverts every biological conclusion.
